HISTORY AND PHYSICAL

CHIEF COMPLAINT: "My sugar has been high and I feel awful."

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
29-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes who presents with 2 days of nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and polyuria. She ran out of insulin 3 days ago. She reports fruity-smelling breath and rapid breathing. Denies fever, chest pain, diarrhea. No sick contacts.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Type 1 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed age 12.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS:
1. Insulin glargine 24 units nightly
2. Insulin lispro 1:10 carb ratio with meals
3. Ondansetron 4 mg q6h PRN (prescribed last month)

SOCIAL HISTORY: College student. No tobacco. Drinks alcohol on weekends.

PHYSICAL EXAM:
Vital signs: Temp 98.8 F, HR 122, BP 104/68, RR 28 deep, SpO2 98% RA.
General: Ill-appearing, dehydrated.
HEENT: Dry mucous membranes, fruity breath odor.
Abdomen: Diffuse tenderness without rebound.
Neuro: Alert, oriented x3.

LABORATORY RESULTS:
Labs: Glucose 684 (H), Na 132 (L), K 5.8 (H), Bicarbonate 8 (L), BUN 34, Creatinine 1.5 (H), A1c 11.2 (H).
ABG: pH 7.18, pCO2 22, HCO3 8.
Urinalysis: large ketones, glucose >1000.

ASSESSMENT: 29-year-old woman with diabetic ketoacidosis precipitated by insulin nonadherence.

PLAN:
1. Diabetic ketoacidosis, severe
- Insulin infusion per DKA protocol, hourly glucose checks
- Aggressive isotonic fluids; add dextrose when glucose <250
- Replace potassium per protocol; monitor q2h BMP, magnesium, phos
2. Hyperglycemia education
- Diabetes education consult before discharge
- Social work for insulin access
